abstract_sentences.text: Large language models are increasingly evaluated as interactive agents, yet standard agent benchmarks conflate two qualitatively distinct sources of success: semantic tool-use and interface-specific interaction pattern memorization.
abstract_sentences.comparison: semantic tool-use versus interface-specific interaction pattern memorization

abstract_sentences.text: Because both mechanisms can yield identical task success on the original interface, benchmark scores alone are not identifiable evidence of environment-invariant capability.
abstract_sentences.comparison: identical original-interface success versus different capability mechanisms

abstract_sentences.text: We propose PIPE, a protocol-level evaluation augmentation for diagnosing interface reliance by minimally rewriting environment interfaces while preserving task semantics and execution behavior.
abstract_sentences.comparison: rewritten interface while task semantics and execution remain

abstract_sentences.text: Across 16 environments from AgentBench and AgentGym and a range of open-source and API-based agents, PIPE reveals that trajectory-SFT substantially amplifies interface shortcutting: trained agents degrade sharply under minimal interface rewrites, while non-trajectory-trained models remain largely stable.
abstract_sentences.comparison: trained agents versus non-trajectory-trained models under minimal rewrites

abstract_sentences.text: We further introduce Interface Reliance (IR), a counterbalanced alias-based metric that quantifies preference for training-time interfaces, and show that interface shortcutting exhibits environment-dependent, non-monotonic training dynamics that remain invisible under standard evaluation.
abstract_sentences.transition: adds a quantitative diagnostic and temporal claim

abstract_sentences.text: Our code is available at Here.

experimental_design.name: Research questions
experimental_design.description: Q1 tests whether PIPE raises intrinsic task difficulty; Q2 tests SFT interface dependence; later sections state Q3 failure analysis and Q4 IR quantification.

evidence.anchor: Our goal is to answer two questions

experimental_design.name: Environment coverage
experimental_design.description: AgentBench and AgentGym cover 16 environments; Tables 7 and 8 give task counts, interaction styles, interfaces, and metrics.

experimental_design.name: Three interface conditions
experimental_design.description: Each agent is evaluated on Original, synonym Perturb 1, and symbol Perturb 2 interfaces; s0, s1, s2, and Delta are reported.

experimental_design.name: Semantic-preservation control
experimental_design.description: Synonyms are described as independently cross-reviewed for semantic equivalence; display-side rewrite and server-side translation leave the backend unchanged.

experimental_design.name: Strict perturbation policy
experimental_design.description: The wrapper rejects an original identifier under perturbation as invalid/deprecated instead of allowing fallback to memorized names.

evidence.anchor: disallow the agent from using the original interface

experimental_design.name: AgentBench agents
experimental_design.description: Compares API GPT models against AgentLM and AgentFLAN trained from AgentBench interaction trajectories.

experimental_design.name: AgentGym before/after training
experimental_design.description: States that Qwen3-8B/14B and Gemma3-4B/12B are fine-tuned on AgentTraj and compared before versus after training.

experimental_design.name: Outcome aggregation
experimental_design.description: For an environment, score is the average task outcome; Delta averages the two perturbation scores relative to Original.

experimental_design.name: IR counterbalance
experimental_design.description: Dual aliases are co-present; original-first and synonym-first prompt orders are run, then log-domain scores are averaged.

experimental_design.name: Training and implementation detail
experimental_design.description: Appendix K lists full-parameter SFT, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, bfloat16, Adam, 1e-5 learning rate, cosine decay, warmup 0.1, batch 2, accumulation 2, and val size=0.

experimental_design.name: Seeds, repeated training, and hardware inventory
experimental_design.description: No seed count, repeated-run count, or hardware model/count is reported in the visible main text or Appendix K; only multi-GPU, DeepSpeed, workers, and precision are specified.

limitations.name: Low-discrimination environments
limitations.description: SQLGym and TextCraft have limited action spaces and strong task semantic anchoring; perturbations can expose smaller gaps.

limitations.name: Single-turn protocol boundary
limitations.description: Mind2Web and SQLGym are near single-turn in this protocol, giving fewer opportunities for compounding interface errors and recovery.

final_judgment.single_storyline: 标准原接口 success score 混合 semantic tool use 与 training-interface shortcut；PIPE 仅改接口表面并比较反事实表现，IR 再把别名选择量化。【p.2 §1；p.3–4 §3；p.7 §6】
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留识别问题、PIPE 定义、两类扰动、16 环境的主性能表、IR 主表与训练期曲线；这些对象足以理解诊断链和主要异质性。【p.3–8】
final_judgment.appendix_moves: 逐步 failure trajectories、环境任务卡、完整接口 mappings、IR counterbalance/aggregation 细节、alpha 敏感性、SciWorld 扩展曲线和 training hyperparameters 迁入附录；复现实装与部分机制解释因此依赖 p.12–31。【p.12–31】
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 先把潜在机制差异变成可读的反事实识别规则，Tables 1–2 给 outcome evidence，Tables 3–4 给近端 alias-preference evidence，Figure 4 再接训练决策。【p.3 Fig.2；p.5–8】
final_judgment.largest_gap: environment-complexity 的 loose/high-pressure 解释主要是跨环境统计 pattern；论文同时缺少 controlled training ablation、seed-level uncertainty 和真实 checkpoint-selection policy 的下游比较。【p.5 §4.2；p.16 §D；p.20 §K；p.31 Tables 24–25】
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 若论文的关键争议是训练增益的机制，把机制差异转为只改一个表面因子的反事实协议，并同时报告 outcome gap 与机制近端行为量。【p.3–4 §3】
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则要求任务、后端执行、功能描述与成功标准保持不变；single-turn 或低工具多样性环境的扰动区分力会下降，score gap 也不是潜在语义表征的直接测量。【p.3–4 §3；p.15 §C.3–C.4】
